transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump is taking his midterm campaign swing
into more competitive territory.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports Trump will visit Ohio today
after stops in Republican-dominated states.
>> The president is traveling to Vandalia, Ohio,
to support Republican Senator John Husted,
who is facing a tight race
against Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown.
Brown is seeking a comeback after losing his Senate seat,
while Husted is a relatively new incumbent.
He has served in the Senate for just two years
after being appointed to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance
when Vance became vice president.
Ohio could offer an early test of how Republicans
in swing states navigate Trump heading into these midterms.
They can either embrace the president
and use his ability to energize the Republican base
or create some distance from him to appeal to more moderate voters.
Trump is expected to travel to Nebraska next,
another heavily red state.
Franco Ordonez in PR News, the White House.
>> A new court filing details the condition of the Tennessee woman
who officials attempted to execute earlier this week.
Attorneys for Christa Pike say she was placed on a ventilator
and remained unconscious as hospital staff worked to save her life.
Tony Gonzalez of member station WPLN in Nashville reports.
>> Christa Pike's legal team wants the Tennessee Department of Correction
to preserve evidence and is asking a judge for help.
They're also citing several months of warnings they had provided
about a blood disorder that would make it difficult to insert an IV line.
They were also concerned because prison staff had failed to insert a line
during another lethal injection attempt in May.
Now they say that the drug pentobarbital
could have been sent into Pike's arm instead of her vein.
Tennessee has struggled with lethal injections.
Four years ago, officials were found to have ignored protocols
and mishandled drugs.
For NPR News, I'm Tony Gonzalez in Nashville.
>> Diesel prices continue to climb,
adding to the cost of getting kids to school.
Colorado Public Radio's Ray Solomon reports
nine out of 10 school buses in the U.S. run on diesel,
which hit a record high last month.
>> The soaring cost of diesel fuel is hitting school districts
where it hurts right in the transportation budget.
Nathan Reimer is transportation director
in the Jefferson County School District near Denver, Colorado.
>> You know, I didn't budget for a war in Iran to affect my diesel prices.
>> But some school districts have alternative bus fleets
that run on electricity or fuels like propane,
and they haven't been affected by high diesel costs.
Most of those districts got federal funding
for these school buses from the 2021 infrastructure law.
The Trump administration halted that program earlier this year,
calling it, quote, "a disaster of wasteful spending."
For NPR News, I'm Ray Solomon in Boulder, Colorado.
>> This is "NPR News."
The price of jet fuel has reached a record high.
According to Airlines for America,
the national average is about $4.39 per gallon.
Kayak says domestic airfares now average more than $400.
That's the highest level this year.
Major League Baseball's divisional round of playoffs
gets underway today with games in four cities.
In Milwaukee, the Brewers will face the San Diego Padres
in a matchup that raises questions about
how much a team's payroll determines its ability to compete.
Chuck Wernbach reports.
>> The Brewers have the best record in baseball
during the regular season,
despite having the smallest market size
and a payroll in the bottom half of Major League clubs.
The Padres payroll is in the top third,
but Milwaukee fan John Mattis says his team
can win the best of five series
because it has more heart and manager Pat Murphy.
>> He does something right with those guys.
I mean, he's got the right attitude.
He leads them well. He does good things with them.
>> A possible salary cap and the competitive balance
are expected to be controversial issues
during a potential labor dispute
after this month's World Series.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Wernbach in Milwaukee.
>> NPR has learned that the U.S. Coast Guard
says it's searching off the coast of Nantucket this morning
for a missing jet carrying six people.
The Gulf Stream aircraft was flying from Bermuda to Boston.
Officials say the FAA lost contact with the plane
early this morning.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.
[music]

topics.text: President Trump campaigns in Ohio to support Republican Senator John Husted against Democrat Sherrod Brown
Tennessee execution of Christa Pike halted; attorneys say lethal injection drugs may have missed vein
Rising diesel fuel prices strain school district transportation budgets across the United States
Jet fuel prices reach record high of $4.39 per gallon, domestic airfares average over $400
Milwaukee Brewers face San Diego Padres in MLB divisional playoffs despite lower payroll
U.S. Coast Guard searches off Nantucket for missing Gulf Stream aircraft with six people
